subject: FastFrame renewal: capacity uplift + competitive trial (benchmark request)
messages:
From: Lena Ortiz <lena.ortiz@fastframe.ai>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 20 Oct 2026 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: FastFrame renewal & capacity uplift

Hi Hannah,

We're coming up on our January renewal and the product team has started a 6-week trial with a competitor (they asked for a parallel evaluation). Early signals: their config handled our peak inference patterns in the POC, but we haven't finished benchmarking latency and cost per token.

We expect to need ~3x current capacity starting Feb 1 if the feature release ships. Before we make any decisions, procurement asked for:
- a short benchmark plan we can run (48–72h) against our workload (we'll provide a sample traffic trace)
- updated pricing for a 36-month committed uplift + breakpoints for dedicated capacity
- a simple mutual action plan and timeline for a canary migration

Can you put someone on this? We're on a tight timeline — procurement expects draft terms by Nov 5.

Thanks,
Lena Ortiz
Head of Platform Ops
FastFrame

Attachment: FastFrame_Renewal_Context.pdf (summary)

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Lena Ortiz <lena.ortiz@fastframe.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 20 Oct 2026 10:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: FastFrame renewal & capacity uplift

Hi Lena — thanks for the heads up and context. We'll prioritize this.

Quick plan:
- Ben will scope a 48h throughput + latency run using your trace; we'll run it on a dedicated canary pool to mirror your peak sequences.
- Marissa will draft a 36-month committed pricing ladder and a short mutual action plan (MAP) for the canary + full roll.
- I'll coordinate SOC2 artifacts and timeline with procurement.

We can share a draft MAP + benchmark protocol by Nov 3 and a pricing term sheet by Nov 5. Can you confirm who on your side will own the trace and give us a point person for procurement (cc Daniel Park if appropriate)?

I'll attach a template MAP to speed things up.

— Hannah
Director, Customer Growth | Redwood Inference
Attachment: FastFrame_Mutual_Action_Plan.xlsx

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 20 Oct 2026 11:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: FastFrame renewal & capacity uplift — benchmark scope

Hannah/Marissa —

I took a quick look at FastFrame's figures from last quarter. Proposal for the benchmark:
1) 48-hour continuous run
2) Two profiles: (A) peak-sustained (90th pct seq length, concurrency target 80% of their declared peak), (B) mixed production trace (they'll provide)
3) Success criteria: 95th latency under 220ms for generation endpoint, no more than 0.6% error rate under load, and cost-per-1M-tokens delta vs their current baseline.

We can provision a dedicated 6-GPU canary cluster for the test. If they commit to a 36-mo uplift at >= 3x baseline, we can offer an introductory uplift credit equal to 1 month at the new committed rate and a staged price break at +2x and +4x.

I'll run the throughput test and produce a short PDF report. Need the trace and a list of model variants they want included.

-Ben
Sr. Account Solutions | Redwood Inference
Attachment: throughput-report-q4.pdf

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Lena Ortiz <lena.ortiz@fastframe.ai>, Daniel Park <daniel.park@fastframe.ai>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 22 Oct 2026 08:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Proposed MAP & term highlights for capacity uplift

Hi Lena/Daniel —

Thanks for agreeing to the benchmark. Attached is a concise MAP and a term highlights sheet. Key points:
- Canary benchmark window: Nov 8–10 (48h); Redwood provides instrumentation and a post-run report within 48h.
- Commercial: 36-month commitment with a three-tiered break point (baseline x2, x3, x4). We can add 1-month credit at contract signature, and a usage-based true-up cadence every quarter.
- Operational: Fast onboarding (2 weeks) if SOC2 docs are accepted; otherwise add 2–3 weeks for compliance review.

To keep pace with the competitor POC, we'd like to run the canary the week of Nov 8. Procurement requested a redline-ready SOW — Ben, can you help with the resource and GPU sizing notes?

Best,
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference
Attachment: redline_sow_v2.docx

From: Daniel Park <daniel.park@fastframe.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Cc: FastFrame Procurement <procurement@fastframe.ai>
Date: Mon, 25 Oct 2026 13:17:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Proposed MAP & term highlights for capacity uplift

Marissa — appreciate the fast turnaround. Procurement has a couple of asks before we sign off on the MAP:
- SOC2 in-scope evidence and logs retention policy
- A short SLI/SLO appendix for the canary (latency targets and incident remediation window)
- DocuSign-ready SOW + PO flow; procurement needs pricing broken out by HW tier

We can provide the traffic trace by Nov 1. We're comfortable with the Nov 8 window if Redwood can commit to the instrumentation and the 48h report turnaround.

Procurement will route the SOW internally once we have a DocuSign link.

Thanks,
Daniel
Platform Engineering Manager | FastFrame

Attachment: (none)

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 01 Nov 2026 14:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Heads-up: FastFrame renewal could need executive approval for concession

Evelyn — quick note. FastFrame (mid-market SaaS) is running a competitor POC and expects a 3x uplift if the feature ships. Procurement wants draft terms by Nov 5 and the canary is Nov 8–10.

We can meet the timeline and instrumentation asks, but procurement expects:
- an introductory uplift credit (1 month) and staged price breaks at 2x/3x/4x
- a commitment to a short incident remediation SLA for the canary

This is within our normal commercial levers but may require your sign-off if they push for an additional concession (extra credit or extended support). If the benchmark shows a performance delta vs the competitor, this could be a net-new expansion opportunity.

Do you want me to schedule a quick 15-min sync later today to run the specific numbers and the potential incremental margin impact?

— Hannah
Director, Customer Growth | Redwood Inference
